core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aasifah corresponds to the Arabic form عاصفة and is glossed in this record as “Storm, tempest, strong wind.” The record associates the form with root ع ص ف (ʿ-ṣ-f). The record identifies the form as feminine. The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Aasifah corresponds to the Arabic form عاصفة (Arabic root ع ص ف (ʿ-ṣ-f); عَاصِفَة (ʿāṣifah)). Its core sense is storm, tempest; strong wind. Aasifah is Arabic عَاصِفَة (ʿāṣifah) 'Storm, tempest, strong wind', the established word for a storm, from the root ع ص ف (ʿ-ṣ-f); it is also the feminine of the active participle عَاصِف (ʿāṣif, 'stormy') of عَصَفَ (ʿaṣafa, 'to storm, to rage'). Aasifah is a variant romanization of Aasfa.
